title: Exponential Quantum Speedup for DDT-Based Attacks
summary: DDTs can be sampled efficiently classically, obstructing a direct transfer of Simon's advantage; whether any DDT-based attack can achieve an exponential quantum speedup remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a function $F$, its DDT can be sampled efficiently by choosing random plaintexts $x_1$ and $x_2$ and obtaining $(\Delta_I,\Delta_O)=(x_1\oplus x_2,F(x_1)\oplus F(x_2))$. This efficient classical sampling is a fundamental obstacle to transferring Simon's exponential quantum speed-up, which does not automatically apply to DDT-based attacks. Determine whether a DDT-based cryptanalytic attack can nevertheless achieve an exponential quantum speed-up over its corresponding classical attack and, if so, how it overcomes this sampling barrier.

scope.domain: Quantum differential cryptanalysis of difference distribution tables and quantum-versus-classical attack complexity.
parameters: F: the function defining the DDT
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a DDT-based cryptanalytic attack can achieve an exponential quantum speedup over its classical counterpart and, if so, how it can overcome efficient classical DDT sampling.

citations.label: A Geometric Approach to Quantum Distinguishers

progress.summary: The paper recovers a quadratic speedup for a DDT-supported quantum distinguisher and then poses exponential speedup as a natural question. It identifies efficient classical DDT sampling as the barrier and rules out a direct Simon/Bernstein–Vazirani-style sampling route without proving a general impossibility.
citation_labels: Zhili Wu et al., A Geometric Approach to Quantum Distinguishers
